properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, on why he built the content store in the first place: \"one of the primary reasons I had also developed the blob was to capture actual agent session context. from my limited understanding, an agent is stateless because it can't recall previous session's context. by storing in the blob, I thought I could make a session 'stateful'. ... however, every decision that an agent makes and implements is already embedded in the graph because it is already using reflow2, therefore, ingesting session context is moot or not needed?\"

⭐ THE QUESTION HAS A RECORDED ANSWER ALREADY, and it is sharper than either yes or no. cap:session-memory (PLANNED, framing settled by Anthony himself on 2026-07-25) states it directly: \"Decision.rationale and ChangeEvent already capture fragments of the why; WHAT LIVES ONLY IN THE SESSION IS THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE — what was tried, what was rejected and on what grounds, which findings turned up while doing something else.\"

So the split is:
  MOOT — the design content. Decisions, their rationale, requirements, changes, snapshots, questions and answers all land in the graph as they happen. Storing a transcript to preserve those would be a second copy of something already held better.
  NOT MOOT — the connective tissue. What was attempted and abandoned, what failed and why, what cost more than expected, what was noticed sideways. None of that is design intent, so none of it has a natural node, and it is precisely what a later session needs in order not to repeat the work.

⭐⭐ THIS SESSION IS THE EVIDENCE, and it is self-implicating rather than hypothetical. 2026-08-09 produced a great deal of design content, all of it now in the graph. It also produced process knowledge that is in NONE of it: hashing an artifact before the last edit FIVE times (because every mandatory gate — fmt, a clippy fix, a skill_lint trim — mutates the file AFTER the work looks finished); piping a gate into `tail` so the pipe returned tail's exit code and a red gate was pushed past; merging a four-PR stack in one loop so three PRs landed in already-squashed base branches and were stranded while GitHub reported all four as MERGED. **Every one of those lives in a markdown memory file OUTSIDE reflow2 entirely.** That is the connective tissue cap:session-memory names, currently housed in exactly the kind of file dec:what-lives-where was written to retire.

=== AND THE PART THAT BEARS ON THE BLOB ===

THE STORE WAS NEVER THE RIGHT MECHANISM FOR THIS, AND cap:session-memory ALREADY SAYS SO: \"a pointer to a 3 MB transcript is a RECEIPT, not documentation: leaning on it recreates the markdown problem one level down, since 'it is all in the transcript' is the same excuse as 'it is all in the backlog file'.\"

Its actual design needs no content store at all: session takeaways as FIRST-CLASS GRAPH CONTENT, written when they happen, anchored to the session's epoch, queryable afterwards. The transcript is modelled as a Fragment carrying the session UUID as portable identity — A POINTER, NOT BYTES — with the absolute path explicitly demoted to a machine-scoped hint, because a path stored as identity resolves for one person and silently misses for everyone else.

⇒ SO THE SESSION-CONTEXT JUSTIFICATION FOR THE BLOB DOES NOT SURVIVE, but not for the reason the question proposes. It is not that session context is worthless — it is that ITS VALUE IS IN DISTILLED NODES, WHICH NEED NO STORE. Storing the transcript would preserve the receipt and lose the documentation.

THE FRAMING THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN CLEANUP, and it is Anthony's own from 2026-07-25: a session's context IS documentation — the how-and-why record of a design's evolution — and documentation is part of the product. That changes the standard rather than the mechanism: \"a convenience can be skipped under load, a deliverable cannot.\"

=== WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN ===

(1) IS THE STATELESSNESS PREMISE ALREADY ANSWERED? reflow2's whole pitch is that the graph is the memory (req:persistence). If so, a transcript store would be a SECOND, lossier memory competing with the first — and two sources of truth is the failure this project designs out everywhere else. That reading says the blob's session justification was solving a problem reflow2 already solves.

(2) WHAT FORCES THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE TO BE WRITTEN? cap:session-memory names this as its load-bearing gap: \"the existing handoff enforcement watches the modification time of MARKDOWN files, so the only mechanism forcing a session to leave takeaways behind POINTS AWAY FROM THE GRAPH.\" That is still true today — it is why this session's process findings are in a memory file. Fixing it is a nudge/hook question, not a storage question.

(3) DOES PROCESS KNOWLEDGE BELONG IN A DESIGN GRAPH AT ALL? Honest counter, recorded beside rather than argued down: \"I hashed before running fmt\" is not design intent. It may belong to the harness or to a project's own working notes, and forcing it into the design graph could make the graph a log — which is the failure mode dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written warns about from the other direction. cap:session-memory's answer is the documentation reframe; whether that reframe holds for PROCESS failures as well as DESIGN reasoning is genuinely unsettled.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Anthony asked a question; cap:session-memory remains PLANNED and unchanged.
properties.name: OPEN — if every decision an agent makes is already in the graph, is capturing session context moot? (No, but the part that isn't moot never needed a blob)
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, counters beside the options, nothing promoted.

Deliberately NOT folded into cap:session-memory, and not used to edit it. That capability already holds the answer to the moot question and its framing is Anthony's own; this node records that the question was asked again, what the existing answer is, and the one part that genuinely bears on the content-store decision — that the session-context justification for the blob does not survive, because the value is in distilled nodes rather than stored bytes.

Linked to dec:idea-discontinue-the-content-store because it removes one of that decision's stated motivations, which is a material change to the argument rather than a footnote.
